newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares soar five pct on hopes for new govt.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares soar five pct on hopes for new govt.

text.p: Istanbul shares surged more than five percent in hectic buying at mid-morning on Friday amid growing hopes that a planned secularist coalition government may win a confidence vote in parliament, brokers said.
The IMKB National-100 .XU100 soared 5.2 percent to an all-time trading high of 1,794 at mid-session. It eased slightly to 1,786 at 0820 GMT, up 81 points, or 4.75 percent from Thursday.

Brokers said the resignations of four deputies from the ruling Islamist-conservative coalition parties buoyed Prime Minister-Designate Mesut Yilmaz's chances of winning a confidence vote in his planned alliance to exclude the ruling Islamists.
Three deputies from the conservative Tansu Ciller's True Path Party (DYP) and one deputy from the Islamist Welfare Party (RP) quit their parties this morning.
"Every single resignation from the DYP and RP ranks boosted the prices. The sudden jumps were followed by minor profit-taking waves," said Bulent Sevindik from Karon securities.
